subject: Post-Report Assurance Addendum & Continuity Confirmation for Q1 2027
messages:
From: Liz Morales <liz.morales@retailco.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.inference>
Cc: RetailCo Legal <legal@retailco.com>, AuditOps <auditops@thirdparty-audit.com>
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 09:13:00 -0400
Subject: Request: SOC 2 Type II post-report addendum and controls continuity confirmation

Hi Naomi,

Thanks again for the SOC 2 Type II report you provided earlier this quarter. Our compliance team is running an intake for a customer-facing procurement review and they are asking for an addendum that covers the period since the report end date (report scope ended 2027-03-31). Specifically they want either: a) a current SOC 2 Type II report that extends to present, or b) a signed addendum / continuity statement (often called a bridge letter) confirming no material control changes affecting security and availability since 2027-03-31, plus any evidence you can share (e.g., change log, architecture diagram, KMS rotation evidence).

Could you let us know if Redwood can provide a signed continuity addendum and an estimated delivery date? If you can, please indicate who will sign and whether legal needs to be involved on our side. We have a procurement deadline of 2027-05-20.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Best,
Liz
Liz Morales
Security & Risk Manager
RetailCo

---
Note: this request is used by our vendor intake team — cc'd AuditOps for assistance with file format expectations.

We can provide a signed post-report assurance addendum confirming continuity of controls from 2027-04-01 through 2027-05-12 (covering the immediate post-report period) and include the supporting artifacts you requested. To be transparent, the addendum will be a limited-scope attestation signed by our Head of Trust, with legal countersignature.

Proposed timeline:
- 2027-05-11: Draft addendum and artifact bundle (SOC report, infra change log, KMS rotation summary)
- 2027-05-12: Final sign-off and PDF delivered to you (DocuSign link)

Soojin / Connor — can you confirm availability to review the draft today and whether the infra change log below is export-ready?

Naomi Feldman

Naomi / Connor — I'm on this. Draft language below for the addendum section that RetailCo requested (will be included in a one-page PDF signed by Head of Trust and countersigned by Legal):

"Post-Report Assurance Addendum (Limited Scope): Redwood Inference affirms that, to the best of its knowledge and except as disclosed in the accompanying infra_changes_log.csv, there have been no material changes to controls relevant to the SOC 2 Security and Availability Trust Services Criteria between 2027-04-01 and 2027-05-12 that would reasonably be expected to affect the operating effectiveness of those controls as reported in the SOC 2 Type II report dated 2027-03-31. Supporting artifacts: infra_changes_log.csv, kms-key-rotation-summary.pdf, and the previously issued SOC2_TypeII_20270331.pdf."

Attachments I can assemble today: SOC2_TypeII_20270331.pdf (copy), infra_changes_log.csv (exported with entries through 2027-05-11), kms-key-rotation-summary.pdf (KMS rotation event summary). Connor, can you confirm there were no architecture-level deployments or major config changes in the April–May window that would alter security posture? If anything exists, flag it so we can add a narrow disclosure.

— Soojin
Soojin Lee
Principal Security Engineer
Redwood Inference

Thanks Naomi and Soojin — that draft language looks good. A couple of small requests from our side:

1) Can the addendum explicitly name the signatory (title is fine) and reference the original SOC 2 report date and period so our procurement system can match artifacts automatically?
2) For escalation transparency, RetailCo Legal would prefer the addendum be delivered via DocuSign and include contact details for the person who can attest to the infra_changes_log (for us to follow up if needed).

If you can deliver by COB 2027-05-12 we'll be able to keep our procurement timeline. Appreciate you pulling this together quickly.

Best,
Liz

On a procedural note: AuditOps prefers PDF bundle + a short README (one page) that lists included files and brief descriptions.
